transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-24 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~57 minutes
Attendees: Martin (Redwood AE), Sofia (Redwood SE), Diego (Redwood CSM), Jamal (Arcadia), Priya (Arcadia), Ellen (Arcadia), Samir (Arcadia)

Summary: quick sync on POC run results, proposal for autoscale + scaleback playbook, discuss burst rehearsals and cost tradeoffs. Agreed items: Redwood to propose YAML, Arcadia to run 2-hour staged burst test, follow-on deep-dive on caching.

Topics: results recap; tail-latency spikes during bursts; cold-start vs hot cache behavior; autoscale cooldowns and step-scaling; burst budget; monitoring/alerts; cost delta for burst policies.

--- Transcript body (timestamps approximate) ---
[00:00] Martin: hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. quick agenda, we wanna review last week's pilot data, talk through autoscale playbook and scaleback thresholds, and align on the 2-hour rehearsal.
[00:28] Jamal: cool, yeah we ran the staged workload, we saw the 95th go up during the second hour, and some of the token costs spiked, not sure if that's cache or packing.
[00:45] Sofia: mm-hmm, when you say token costs spiked, do you mean billable tokens per request went up or the per-second throughput dropped?
[00:55] Jamal: both? like our cost per call went up because requests took longer and sometimes doubled in tokens because of repeated re-rolls. transcription: \"re-rolls\" might be mis-phrase here.
[01:12] Priya: and we noticed KV cash misses — uh cache misses — when we routed between regions, maybe our sticky routing wasn't working.
[01:28] Sofia: yeah that matches what we instrumented on our side too; cross-zone routing can evict prefixes from the KV cache and that increases generation tokens.
[01:44] Ellen: is that a thing we can control from the Redwood side with a routing policy? or is it on our infra?
[01:52] Martin: it's a mix. Redwood can suggest model pinning and routing policies to keep session affinity, but you also wanna ensure your load balancer preserves sticky session metadata.
[02:07] Samir: one question — we have a hard budget for burst ops. how do we cap bursts without blowing baseline latency?
[02:15] Sofia: common pattern: step-scaling + a soft budget. e.g., allow 2x baseline for up to 60 minutes, then auto-failover to a cheaper model variant or scale-down. we can encode that in the autoscale policy YAML.
[02:32] Martin: i'll share a couple profiles (fast-high-cost, balanced, cost-saver).
[02:39] Jamal: ok show us the numbers so we can pick one.
[02:45] Sofia: here's a subtlety — cooldown. if cooldown's too long you might keep extra GPUs idle and burn money; if it's too short you thrash and cause oscillation. we recommend a 5-8 minute stabilization window plus a backoff that lengthens after repeated scale events.
[03:05] Priya: does Redwood support step-down scaling that ejects only the extra nodes first? we can't afford to drop core capacity.
[03:12] Sofia: yes, policy supports prioritized node removal — we label pools as baseline vs burst and scaleback removes from burst pool first.
[03:22] Jamal: in the run we saw a weird lat spike around minute 73 when we did a simulated traffic shift. logs show KV cache thrash, several model proxies reloaded. maybe the kernel selections stuttered.
[03:36] Martin: that aligns with our thesis — kernel selection and quantized fallback paths can add jitter during unusual seq lengths. Diego, you had the perf charts?
[03:45] Diego: yes, i'll paste later but 90th and 95th tail are where we see most variance; avg token latency stayed ok. the memory pressure on GPUs spiked when bursts exceeded batch windows.
[03:59] Priya: can we pre-warm KV caches or pin hot prefixes?
[04:05] Sofia: you can pre-warm by replaying typical session prefixes into the cache; also you can enable prefix caching TTLs to be longer for critical routes. note: longer TTLs mean more memory usage.
[04:20] Ellen: any quick wins to reduce cost for the next rehearsal?
[04:25] Martin: short term: reduce model size for non-essential paths, enable prefix caching for top 20 routes, and bump burst cooldown to 7 minutes. medium term: tune batching windows.
[04:37] Samir: what about cold start penalties for new inference containers in Dedicated? we run in dedicated pool and saw warmup times of ~8-10s for some models.
[04:47] Sofia: warm starts are a thing — we recommend keeping a small baseline of hot instances per SKU; that's the baseline pool. burst instances can be cheap and cold, but you pay the start penalty.
[05:00] Jamal: cost math — can you send us delta between 2x and 3x burst for our current profile?
[05:06] Martin: yep, i'll model that and send before Friday.
[05:10] Priya: alerting, we need token-level alerts and a budget burn alert. can Redwood expose token-level metrics to our Grafana?
[05:18] Diego: already set up a dashboard for you but we need to grant read access.
[05:22] Martin: we'll provide a token-level telemetry feed and an export link. Diego will set ACLs.
[05:27] Jamal: the other risk is failover — if a region loses capacity, how do we avoid cascading to higher-cost models?
[05:35] Sofia: policy example: prefer local region, then adjacent region, then cheaper model. you can also set a hard cap to stop failover and return 429s instead of paying huge premium. that's an important business decision.
[05:49] Ellen: our product folks prefer graceful degradation rather than errors. they'd rather slower responses than dropped queries.
[05:54] Martin: note that degradation strategy affects SLOs and user experience; we should map user journeys to policy.
[06:02] Jamal: during the burst run, we saw one run where the system fell back to a quantized variant; quality delta was noticeable on longer sequences. can we A/B test that?
[06:12] Sofia: yes, canary fallback with automatic rollback on eval regressions. Redwood Optimize includes model-quality monitoring tied to prompt sets. you can set thresholds per route.
[06:24] Priya: can we have an automated regression alert if rouge-l or edit-distance crosses X?
[06:29] Martin: we typically use a combination of n-gram overlap and human-reviewed prompts; we'll propose thresholds.
[06:36] Jamal: ok, logistics for the 2-hour rehearsal — we plan to do it on staging; timeline target next Wednesday 2026-03-04. we want Redwood to be on standby.
[06:47] Martin: we'll be on hand. Sofia will run pre-check script and provide a checklist.
[06:53] Sofia: pre-checks include: baseline pool size, TTL for prefix cache, batch window target, and baseline telemetry snapshot. i'll share checklist.
[07:05] Samir: if the rehearsal reveals more cache thrash, what's the remediation action?
[07:11] Sofia: immediate: increase baseline hot instances and enable session affinity; follow-up: analyze prefix distribution and implement targeted pre-warm.
[07:20] Ellen: about the autoscale YAML, can you show the backoff curve and where we cap total GPUs?
[07:27] Sofia: yes i'll include a graph; typical curve: thresholds at 60%, 75%, 90% utilization with step sizes of +20%, +30%, +50% respectively and a hard cap at 3x baseline unless overridden.
[07:43] Jamal: we need a manual override channel — our SRE should be able to flip a kill-switch if costs explode.
[07:50] Martin: we support manual overrides via Console and API keys, and we can add an SSO ACL for your SREs.
[07:58] Priya: security note: we need SOC two and audit logs for these operations. do you have an SOC 2 report?
[08:06] Martin: yes, we have SOC 2 Type II, and we can share the attestation and audit log export docs.
[08:13] Jamal: ok next — instrumentation. we saw correlating events but need trace-level linking between client request ID and GPU allocation. can Redwood surface that?
[08:24] Sofia: yes, we can pass request IDs through the runtime and the Console will show per-request lifecycle events; that will help debug allocation anomalies.
[08:33] Ellen: are there any gotchas for on-prem private deploys? not for us now but curious.
[08:39] Martin: on-prem means you manage the infra, we provide control plane; KV cache behavior and network topology are more in your control so you'd need to tune affinity more carefully.
[08:50] Jamal: last quick question — our procurement asked if we could commit to a short-term Dedicated minimum if rehearsal goes well. what's typical?
[08:58] Diego: we have monthly reserved pools; pilots often convert to a 3–6 month commit with a ramp. terms can be discussed with Sales.
[09:08] Martin: recap — action owners and due dates captured; next sync after rehearsal to review logs and cost impact.
[09:15] Jamal: thanks all.
[09:18] Martin: thanks, we'll follow up with YAML, scripts and the cost models.

End of transcript.

References shared: link: https://redwood.example.com/pilot/arcadia-burst-report (redwood internal link), autoscale-playbook-v2 (doc), rehearsal-checklist.csv (note).

Notes on transcription: some proper nouns garbled (KV cash -> KV cache, SOC two -> SOC 2), speaker labels simplified.
